The Minister for Water Resources stated at a press conference that the plant will provide "clean water to one million citizens," claiming that the project "ends decades of thirst." He added that the government "will not allow any delay." [...] A local newspaper reported, citing a source of the ministry whose identity it did not reveal, that the real cost could exceed billion dollars due to the increase in material prices. This information could not be verified at an independent source. According to environmental experts, desalination is a necessary solution in a region suffering from drought, but warns against its consequences on marine life if the brine produced is not properly treated. The Ministry's statement makes no reference to an environmental impact study. 11 · Example. a) Analysis report. References. Article of local chronicle (invented), Republic of the Sea, without signature. Summary. The Ministry of Water has announced the signing of a contract from 800 million dollars with a consortium of foreign and local companies to build a desalination plant on the southern coast, operating within three years. Sources and positions. The Minister presents the project in emphatic terms (the end of decades of thirst, no delay). Local associations question the calendar, recalling a similar project announced six years ago and never realized, and ask for the full publication of the contract. A local newspaper reports, quoting an anonymous source of the ministry, that the cost could exceed a billion: unverified information. Environmental experts consider desalination necessary, but warn of risks to the marine environment if brine is not treated. Opinions and connotations. The title quotes the government slogan "the end of thirst" ( ⁧نهاية العطش⁩ ) and contrasts it with the expectation of the inhabitants. Lacune and signals. No environmental impact study, company names or contract conditions are mentioned; There is no independent source of cost.
